items.text: Demarcation point identified and photographed; customer-side scope separated from provider plant.
Primary protector (communications circuits / network-powered broadband) installed at the entrance, listed, out of hazardous locations and away from ignitible material.
Protector / sheath / coax shield bonding conductor landed at the intersystem bonding termination where present, otherwise at the nearest 800.100(B) point.
Bonding conductor 14 AWG minimum, not required over 6 AWG, as short and straight as practicable, 20 ft maximum at a one- or two-family dwelling.
Any separate communications electrode bonded back to the power grounding electrode system with 6 AWG minimum.
Metallic sheath of entering communications cable grounded or interrupted by an insulating joint at the entrance; coax shield grounded at its grounding block at the entrance.
Metal entrance conduit bonded to the grounding electrode system.
Communications and coax kept out of power raceways, boxes, and enclosures except a listed barrier/divider setup; 2 in separation kept in open runs.
No communications or coax cable strapped, taped, or tied to the outside of a raceway for support; all runs on their own supports.
Cable types match the space: CMP in plenums, CMR (or a listed protected path) in risers, CM/CMG general use, CMX only within its dwelling limits.
Accessible abandoned communications cable removed; kept spares tagged for future use with durable tags.
All penetrations of rated walls, floors, and ceilings firestopped with an approved system.
At least one communications outlet roughed in a readily accessible area of each new dwelling, cabled to the demarcation point.

Antenna work, where present: mast grounded per 810.21, discharge unit at the entrance, bonding conductor 10 AWG copper minimum, lead-in clearances kept (2 ft / 10 ft / 6 ft from lightning conductors).
Communications entrance planned at the service location so the bond lands with the meter/panel layout instead of a remote rod.
Photograph every finished entrance bond (protector, coax block, broadband, dish) before it is covered or buried behind provider equipment.
